transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, well, I came in today because I just can’t seem to shake this really heavy, hopeless feeling. It's... it's like everything I built up after my divorce has just completely collapsed, and I’m just sitting under it. I don't know how else to describe it, but I just can't seem to get out from under it, and that's why I'm here.
Can you tell me approximately when these heavy, hopeless feelings started, and how long they've been going on since then?
Um, I'd say it's been going on for about a month now. It really started right around the time all the financial mess from the divorce hit, and... yeah, it's just been hanging over me ever since.
Over this past month, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I still care about the things I usually like to do. I still try to do them... it's just that this heavy feeling is always there hanging over me while I do. But I wouldn't say I've lost interest in them.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep over this past month, such as trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

Yeah, my sleep has definitely been affected. Um, lately I either just lie awake staring at the ceiling, kind of replaying all the bills and work mistakes in my head... or I'll wake up way before dawn and feel like I never actually slept at all. So, yeah, I'm definitely having trouble with it.

Would you say this heavy, hopeless feeling is mainly tied to thinking about the divorce and the financial situation, or has it spread into affecting how you feel about other areas of your life as well?

I think it's really just tied to the divorce and the money. I haven't noticed it spreading to everything else, honestly. Like I mentioned, I still care about the things I normally do... it's just the financial stuff that's constantly weighing on my mind right now.
Have you been experiencing feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt about yourself during this past month?

Yes, definitely. I just... I keep telling myself that I'm a terrible engineer, a failed wife, and honestly, just a burden to everyone. I find myself constantly replaying every missed calculation at work or every tense email I've sent, and it just feels like proof that I ruin things. So, yeah, I've been feeling a lot of guilt and like I'm just not worth much right now.
Have you ever had a similar period of low mood, hopelessness, or depression like this at any other point in your life, before the divorce?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days or stressful weeks here and there, like anyone else, but... no, I've never felt anything like this before. This is the first time it's been this bad.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over the past month?
No, not really. I think I'm eating about the same as I usually do. My clothes still fit the same, so I haven't noticed any weight changes either.
Over this past month, have you had any thoughts of wanting to hurt yourself or that you'd be better off not being here?

Yes. I've been having thoughts that... well, that it would just be easier if I didn't wake up. It got to a point where the thoughts were so intense that I actually scared myself. That's what made me finally call the employee assistance program at work.
Over this past month, have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy, even when you haven't been especially active?

Yes. It's been really bad. Getting through a normal workday just feels like dragging wet concrete. I haven't been doing anything extra, but even basic things... like taking a shower or just opening my laptop... it takes way more energy than I seem to have right now. I'm just completely drained.
How has this been affecting your ability to function at work and manage your daily responsibilities—are you still able to keep up, or has it become very difficult to get through the day?

It's been really difficult, to be honest. I'm definitely not keeping up. At work, I was making some pretty questionable calls on my projects, and... well, I was just falling apart in meetings. My supervisor actually had to step in and take me off all active project decisions. 

And at home, it's the same. I completely stopped keeping up with my basic routines. Like I said before about the thoughts getting so bad... it actually escalated to where I ended up being sent to the emergency department, just because I really didn't feel safe with my own thoughts anymore.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a single, first-episode depressive syndrome of one month's duration, precipitated by a clear psychosocial stressor (divorce/financial collapse). She endorses depressed mood, significant insomnia (both initial and early morning awakening), marked fatigue/anergia, feelings of worthlessness and excessive guilt, impaired concentration/decision-making (reflected in work errors), and active suicidal ideation severe enough to prompt an ED visit. These symptoms have caused marked functional impairment at work (removed from active projects) and at home (unable to maintain routines). No psychotic features (hallucinations/delusions) were elicited, ruling out F32.3. While stressor-related, the symptom burden (6+ core depressive symptoms including suicidality) and severity exceed what would be expected for an adjustment disorder (F43.21), supporting a diagnosis of a single severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms (F32.2).
